```{r setup, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(kelpbio)
library(dplyr)
library(posterior)
```

This article covers what lies beyond the main workflow in
`vignette("kelpbio")`: working with posterior draws directly, choosing rows to
predict at, changing priors, checking a fit, and controlling the sampler. The
bundled pre-fits stand in for fitted models; calls that run the sampler are
shown but not run.

## Working with draws

### The draws column

The derived verbs (`kb_predict_mean_weight()`, `kb_predict_biomass_in_situ()`,
and `kb_predict_biomass_canopy()`) return their response as a column of
posterior draws, a `posterior` `rvar`, next to `estimate`, `lower`, and
`upper`. Arithmetic on an `rvar` is done draw by draw, so any quantity built
from it carries the full posterior uncertainty.

```{r}
set.seed(1)
biomass <- kb_predict_biomass_in_situ(
  fit_weight_sim_nereo,
  fit_size_sim_nereo,
  data_in_situ_sim_nereo,
  progress = "none"
)
biomass$biomass_kg_m2[1:3]
```

### Summaries other than pooling

`pool_by` pools rows by summing biomass, and per area divides by the summed
area. Other summaries come from summarising the draws column. The unweighted
mean biomass per m² of the surveys in each site-year, giving each survey the
same weight whatever its area:

```{r}
biomass |>
  group_by(site, year) |>
  summarise(mean_kg_m2 = rvar_mean(biomass_kg_m2), .groups = "drop")
```

`rvar_mean()`, `rvar_sum()`, `rvar_median()`, `rvar_min()`, and `rvar_max()`
summarise across rows within each draw. Summarise the draws, not the
`estimate`, `lower`, and `upper` columns: the sum or mean of limits is not the
limit of the sum or mean.

### Comparisons and probabilities

Differences, ratios, and probabilities between groups also come from the
draws. Total biomass by year, the change from 2019 to 2022, and the
probability that biomass was higher in 2022:

```{r}
set.seed(1)
totals <- kb_predict_biomass_canopy(
  fit_cover_calibration_sim_nereo,
  data_canopy_sim_nereo,
  pool_by = "year"
)
by_year <- setNames(totals$biomass_kg, totals$year)
by_year["2022"] / by_year["2019"]
Pr(by_year["2022"] > by_year["2019"])
```

`quantile2()`, `median()`, `mean()`, and `sd()` summarise an `rvar` over its
draws; `posterior::summarise_draws()` gives several at once.

### The posterior of a fit

`kb_samples()` and `posterior::as_draws()` return a fit's draws as a
`draws_rvars` object, and the other `posterior` conversions accept a fit:

```{r}
draws <- kb_samples(fit_weight_sim_nereo)
draws$diameter_power
summarise_draws(fit_weight_sim_nereo) |>
  head()
```

The `rstantools` generics give draws-by-rows matrices for any rows:
`posterior_linpred()` (the linear predictor), `posterior_epred()` (the
expected response), and `posterior_predict()` (new observations, with the
model's observation noise).

```{r}
rows <- data.frame(diameter_mm = c(20, 40, 60))
epred <- posterior_epred(fit_weight_sim_nereo, rows)
dim(epred)
```

## Rows to predict at

`kb_new_data()` builds grids by site, year, or both, crossed with values of a
model's predictor:

```{r}
grid <- kb_new_data(fit_weight_sim_nereo, by = "site", diameter_mm = c(30, 50))
head(grid)
```

A site or year that the fit has no data for is a new level. `new_levels`
says how its effect is treated: `"average"` takes the typical site or year,
and `"sample"` draws a new effect from the estimated variation, so the
interval covers that variation too. `representative_site` gives a new site
the effects of fitted sites instead:

```{r}
new_site <- data.frame(diameter_mm = 40, site = "new_reef", year = "2021")
kb_predict_weight(fit_weight_sim_nereo, new_site, new_levels = "average")
kb_predict_weight(
  fit_weight_sim_nereo,
  new_site,
  representative_site = "otter_cove"
)
```

The derived verbs default to `"sample"`, since their rows are particular
site-years; the model verbs default to `"average"`.

## Priors

Each model has a list of default priors, one entry per parameter, named as in
`tidy()`:

```{r}
kb_priors_cover_calibration_nereo()
```

A list passed to `priors` replaces only the entries it names; the family of
each entry is fixed, and its hyperparameters can be changed:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
fit <- kb_fit_cover_calibration_nereo(
  biomass,
  priors = list(cover_slope = kb_prior_lognormal(meanlog = 2, sdlog = 0.5))
)
```

`prior_summary()` returns the priors a fit used:

```{r}
prior_summary(fit_cover_calibration_sim_nereo)
```

### Prior predictive checks

A fit with `prior_only = TRUE` samples from the priors alone, ignoring the
data. Its posterior predictive check is a prior predictive check: whether the
priors allow data like those observed.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
prior_fit <- kb_fit_weight_nereo(data_weight_sim_nereo, prior_only = TRUE)
pp_check(prior_fit)
```

### Prior sensitivity

`kb_sensitivity()` power-scales the prior and the likelihood (with the
priorsense package) and flags the parameters whose posterior depends strongly
on the prior or on weak data:

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("priorsense", quietly = TRUE)}
kb_sensitivity(fit_weight_sim_nereo)
```

## Checking a fit

- `kb_converged()` checks Rhat, effective sample sizes, and divergences
  against thresholds that can be set; `summary()` adds the per-parameter
  diagnostics and the sampler footer.
- `pp_check()` overlays replicate datasets on the observed data, or with
  `type = "residual"` the deviance residuals.
- `loo()` and `loo_compare()` estimate and compare out-of-sample predictive
  accuracy from the stored draws, and `kb_influence()` lists the observations
  with high Pareto k.
- `kb_model_describe()` prints the fitted model, and `kb_stancode()` its Stan
  source.

```{r}
kb_converged(fit_weight_sim_nereo)
pp_check(fit_weight_sim_nereo, type = "residual")
loo(fit_weight_sim_nereo)
kb_influence(fit_weight_sim_nereo) |>
  filter(influential)
```

`log_lik()` gives the pointwise log-likelihood for the loo package, and the
draws convert for bayesplot:

```{r}
bayesplot::mcmc_trace(
  as_draws_array(fit_weight_sim_nereo),
  pars = c("intercept", "diameter_power")
)
```

## Sampler control

- `chains`, `niters` (saved draws per chain), `nthin`, `cores`, and `seed` set
  the sampling, and `control` (for example `list(adapt_delta = 0.99)`) passes
  through to `rstan::sampling()`.
- Fits combined in a derived verb must have the same number of draws, so fit
  them with the same `chains` and `niters`.
- `progress` sets the console output, and `progress_dir` records progress that
  `kb_progress()` reads from another R process, for example to drive a progress
  bar in an app.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
dir <- tempfile()
dir.create(dir)
fit <- kb_fit_weight_nereo(
  data_weight_sim_nereo,
  chains = 4,
  niters = 1000,
  seed = 1,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99),
  progress = "none",
  progress_dir = dir
)
kb_progress(dir)
```
